hint: Built by Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal in Agra.
fact: The Taj Mahal took 20 years and 20,000 artisans to build (1632–1653 CE).

hint: World's tallest brick minaret, located in Delhi.
fact: At 72.5 metres, the Qutb Minar was begun in 1193 CE and took nearly 200 years to complete.

hint: The 'Palace of Winds' in Jaipur has 953 small windows.
fact: Hawa Mahal was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh so royal ladies could observe street festivals unseen.

hint: The holiest Sikh shrine, located in Amritsar, Punjab.
fact: The Golden Temple feeds over 100,000 people daily for free — the world's largest community kitchen.

hint: A 16th-century mosque and monument with four minarets in Hyderabad.
fact: Charminar was built in 1591 CE by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to commemorate the end of a deadly plague.

hint: A basalt arch monument in Mumbai built to welcome King George V.
fact: Paradoxically, it was the site from which the last British troops left India in 1948.

hint: A war memorial on Rajpath, New Delhi, honouring 84,000 Indian soldiers.
fact: The Amar Jawan Jyoti (Flame of the Immortal Soldier) was added in 1971.

hint: Ancient ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire in Karnataka.
fact: Hampi was the second-largest medieval-era city in the world after Beijing.

hint: A 13th-century CE sun temple at Konark, Odisha, built as a giant chariot.
fact: The temple has 24 intricately carved stone wheels and is led by 7 stone horses.

hint: A large marble building in Kolkata, West Bengal.
fact: It was built between 1906 and 1921 dedicated to the memory of Queen Victoria.

hint: Historic fort in Old Delhi built by Shah Jahan in 1639.
fact: The Prime Minister hoists the Indian flag here every Independence Day.

hint: Historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai.
fact: The temple complex has 14 gopurams (gateway towers), the tallest being 170 feet high.

hint: Group of Hindu and Jain temples in Madhya Pradesh famous for their nagara-style architectural symbolism.
fact: Most Khajuraho temples were built between 950 and 1050 by the Chandela dynasty.

hint: A Buddhist complex, famous for its Great Stupa, on a hilltop at Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh.
fact: It is one of the oldest stone structures in India, originally commissioned by Ashoka.

hint: A historical palace and a royal residence at Mysore in Karnataka.
fact: It is one of the most famous tourist attractions in India, after the Taj Mahal.

hint: Rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE in Maharashtra.
fact: The caves include paintings and rock-cut sculptures described as among the finest surviving examples of ancient Indian art.

hint: An imambara complex in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, built by Asaf-ud-Daula.
fact: It is famous for the incredible Bhulbhulaiya (labyrinth) located on the upper floor.

hint: The mausoleum of King Mohammed Adil Shah in Bijapur, Karnataka.
fact: Its dome is the second largest in the world, and it has an amazing whispering gallery.

hint: A fortified citadel and an early capital city of the Qutb Shahi dynasty in Hyderabad.
fact: It is famous for its acoustic effects; a hand clap at the entrance can be heard at the highest pavilion.

hint: Located in Arunachal Pradesh, it is the largest monastery in India.
fact: Founded in 1680-1681, it is the second largest monastery in the world after the Potala Palace.

hint: An 8th-century hill fort near Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
fact: Emperor Babur described it as 'the pearl amongst fortresses in India'.

hint: One of the largest forts in India, located in Rajasthan, known for the tales of Rani Padmini.
fact: It sprawls over a hill 180 m in height spread over an area of 691.9 acres.

hint: A Hindu temple dedicated to the solar deity Surya located in Gujarat.
fact: It was built after 1026-27 CE during the reign of Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty.

hint: A Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu.
fact: Built by Raja Raja Chola I between 1003 and 1010 CE, it is one of the largest South Indian temples.

hint: An intricately constructed stepwell situated in the town of Patan in Gujarat.
fact: It is designed as an inverted temple highlighting the sanctity of water.

hint: The tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun in Delhi.
fact: Built in 1570, it was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.

hint: An ancient, but much rebuilt and restored, Buddhist temple in Bodh Gaya.
fact: It marks the location where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment.
